cs.AI / 1 / 2610.28629
GBClaw: An agentic AI framework for atomistic grain boundary research and mechanistic discovery
GBClaw：用于原子尺度晶界研究与机理发现的智能体AI框架
Yazhuo Liu, Kunqing Ding, Xiaoguo Gong, Zifeng Wang, Yichen Yang, Yifeng Che, Wen Chen, Josh Kacher, Olivier Pierron, Shigenobu Ogata, Ting Zhu
cond-mat.mtrl-sci · cond-mat.mes-hall · cs.AI · cs.MA
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems hold immense potential for automating complex workflows in materials discovery and design, but extending them to domain-intensive mechanistic investigations remains challenging. Here, we present GBClaw, an agentic AI framework for investigating the structure and deformation of general grain boundaries (GBs). Although general GBs constitute the vast majority of real-world interfaces in polycrystalline materials, they remain understudied because their structural complexity and interfacial mismatch complicate experimental and modeling research. GBClaw integrates large language models (LLMs) into a modular architecture comprising an orchestrator, specialized agents, domain-specific tools, simulation interfaces, and hierarchical memory. Through dynamic replanning and iterative workflow refinement, the framework effectively connects systematic simulations with targeted mechanistic analysis. Applied to 14 general asymmetric tilt GBs in nickel, GBClaw characterized interfacial defect structures and identified diverse deformation modes across these incommensurate boundaries. Comparing boundary sliding with and without secondary GB misfit dislocations revealed substantial differences in shear strength, underscoring the critical role of defect hierarchies in sliding resistance. Furthermore, researcher-guided follow-up calculations traced an anomalously high shear resistance to metastable boundary structures. This work demonstrates that combining agentic AI with domain expertise bridges high-throughput computational screening with deep physical understanding of complex material interfaces.
Chinese Translation
智能体人工智能（AI）系统在实现材料发现与设计中复杂工作流的自动化方面具有巨大潜力，但将其扩展到领域知识密集的机理研究仍然具有挑战性。在此，我们提出GBClaw，一个用于研究一般晶界（GBs）的结构与变形的智能体AI框架。尽管一般晶界构成了多晶材料中真实界面的绝大多数，但由于其结构复杂性和界面失配使实验与建模研究复杂化，它们仍然研究不足。GBClaw将大语言模型（LLMs）集成到一个模块化架构中，该架构包括一个编排器、专门化智能体、领域特定工具、模拟接口和分层记忆。通过动态重新规划和迭代工作流改进，该框架有效地将系统化模拟与有针对性的机理分析连接起来。应用于镍中的14个一般非对称倾转晶界，GBClaw表征了界面缺陷结构，并在这些非公度晶界中识别出多种变形模式。比较有和没有次级晶界错配位错的晶界滑动，揭示了剪切强度的显著差异，凸显了缺陷层级在滑动阻力中的关键作用。此外，研究人员引导的后续计算将异常高的剪切阻力追溯到亚稳晶界结构。这项工作表明，将智能体AI与领域专业知识相结合，能够将高通量计算筛选与对复杂材料界面的深入物理理解连接起来。

cs.AI / 2 / 2610.27120
EDMA: Entropy-Driven Multimodal Answering
EDMA：熵驱动的多模态回答
Emanuele Mezzi, Gertjan Burghouts, Fabio Massacci, Mengyuan Zhang
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Multimodal question answering (MMQA) is based on integrating heterogeneous data sources, selectively leveraging relevant modalities, and ignoring distractors. Existing approaches based on Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) improve performance by splitting the task into intermediate steps, but do not quantify how each modality contributes to reaching the final answer. We argue that quantifying the effect that each modality has on the answering process improves process traceability and final performance. Thus, we propose Entropy-Driven Multimodal Answering (EDMA), which uses logical entropy to formalise multimodal QA as an iterative process of entropy reduction and to quantify the contribution of each modality in distinguishing correct from incorrect candidate answers. This enables the construction of quantifiable answering trajectories, where each step is associated with a measurable entropy reduction. EDMA introduces (i) modality-conditioned partitioning to estimate unimodal entropy reduction, (ii) entropy-driven multimodal fusion to capture complementary information across modalities, and (iii) entropy-based selection of the answering trajectory that minimises the most logical entropy. Evaluated across standard MMQA benchmarks, EDMA outperforms competitive prompting baselines, with average gains of 12.8 F1 and 4.6 LLM-J points over Planning Prompting and 18.6 F1 and 8.3 LLM-J points over Chain-of-Thought. Moreover, EDMA outperforms self-consistency baselines and is competitive with the multi-agent system baseline. Moreover, we show that higher entropy correlates with more false positives and, through controlled trajectory selection, demonstrate that logical entropy serves as an effective, monotonic selector for correct reasoning paths, validating entropy level as a reliable proxy for performance.
Chinese Translation
多模态问答（MMQA）基于集成异构数据源、选择性利用相关模态并忽略干扰项。基于多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）的现有方法通过将任务拆分为中间步骤来提高性能，但没有量化每种模态对得出最终答案的贡献。我们认为，量化每种模态对回答过程的影响可以提高过程可追溯性和最终性能。因此，我们提出熵驱动多模态回答（EDMA），它使用逻辑熵将多模态问答形式化为熵减少的迭代过程，并量化每种模态在区分正确与错误候选答案中的贡献。这使得能够构建可量化的回答轨迹，其中每一步都与可测量的熵减少相关联。EDMA 引入 (i) 模态条件划分以估计单模态熵减少，(ii) 熵驱动的多模态融合以捕获跨模态的互补信息，以及 (iii) 基于熵的选择使最具逻辑性的熵最小化的回答轨迹。在标准 MMQA 基准上评估，EDMA 优于有竞争力的提示基线，相较于 Planning Prompting 平均提升 12.8 F1 和 4.6 LLM-J 点，相较于 Chain-of-Thought 提升 18.6 F1 和 8.3 LLM-J 点。此外，EDMA 优于自一致性基线，并与多智能体系统基线具有竞争力。此外，我们表明更高的熵与更多假阳性相关，并且通过受控轨迹选择，证明逻辑熵可作为正确推理路径的有效单调选择器，从而验证熵水平作为性能的可靠代理指标。

cs.AI / 3 / 2610.27220
Sparse RL Relaxation for LLM Reasoning
面向大语言模型推理的稀疏强化学习松弛
Jiabin Fan, Matthias Lindemann, Zita Marinho, André FT Martins, Lili Mou
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Recent work has explored continuous representations in place of discrete tokens during Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning, often referred to as soft CoT. This is motivated by the idea that a mixture of token embeddings can represent a superposition of multiple reasoning possibilities within a single step. However, it remains challenging to train large language models to realize this potential. Existing work has explored reinforcement learning (RL)-style training for soft CoT. However, these approaches treat soft tokens as actions in a Markov decision process rather than as differentiable intermediate computation steps. Thus, they do not propagate gradients across the soft tokens and miss out on the signal of how the choice of one soft token affects the next. In this paper, we propose a sparse relaxation method for RL (called SpaRLax), which leverages the differentiability of soft-CoT reasoning over time steps and makes training more stable and effective. We adopt an entmax sparsity method that adaptively determines the degree of softness, which truncates long-tail noise at confident steps while retaining multiple plausible candidates when uncertain. Across nine reasoning benchmarks, our method achieves the highest average performance compared with baseline methods. Further analyses validate the effective use of soft-token superposition in our approach, and also demonstrate the contribution of adaptive sparsity in our approach.
Chinese Translation
近期工作探索了在思维链（Chain-of-Thought, CoT）推理过程中用连续表示替代离散词元，这通常被称为软思维链（soft CoT）。其动机在于，词元嵌入的混合可以在单个步骤内表示多种推理可能性的叠加。然而，训练大语言模型以实现这一潜力仍然具有挑战性。现有工作已探索了针对软思维链的强化学习（RL）风格训练。然而，这些方法将软词元视为马尔可夫决策过程中的动作，而不是可微的中间计算步骤。因此，它们不会跨软词元传播梯度，并错失了关于一个软词元的选择如何影响下一个软词元的信号。在本文中，我们提出了一种用于强化学习的稀疏松弛方法（称为SpaRLax），该方法利用软思维链推理在时间步上的可微性，并使训练更加稳定和有效。我们采用了一种entmax稀疏化方法，该方法自适应地确定软度程度，在置信步骤截断长尾噪声，而在不确定时保留多个合理候选。在九个推理基准上，与基线方法相比，我们的方法取得了最高的平均性能。进一步的分析验证了我们方法中软词元叠加的有效使用，也证明了我们方法中自适应稀疏性的贡献。

cs.AI / 4 / 2610.27230
Magnolia: A Persistent-Memory Agent Framework for Computational Chemistry
Magnolia：面向计算化学的持久记忆智能体框架
Tao Jiang, Benjamin Navet, Yousouf Taghzouti, Fabien Gandon, Louis-Félix Nothias, Élise Dumont
cs.AI · q-bio.BM
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Chemistry has recently entered a high-data regime as molecular databases from high-throughput platforms or computational studies have become available. Increasing automation within the chemical sciences leads to a more digital and precision chemistry. Dedicated scientific agents are becoming central to guiding the chemist through an ever-increasing amount of data and findings, including negative ones. Here, we introduce Magnolia, a persistent-memory artificial intelligence agent framework that integrates computational protocols, from docking to quantum chemistry, lab notebooks and chat logs relying on large language models (LLMs). It relies on a three-tier memory system: session-level observations are automatically captured and distilled into structured learnings, confirmed and elevated to project-tier entries and, when human-validated, promoted to cross-project rules that actively guide subsequent work and provide direct chemical feedback. We illustrate Magnolia on four case studies: quantum-chemical evaluation of aromatic systems (COMPAS database), molecular dynamics of butane and of modified DNA, and a protein-peptide docking campaign. Across these projects, Magnolia tracked 317 runs and accumulated 116 project-tier entries, from which four cross-project rules were promoted; in controlled replays of four tasks, runs with memory passed the checks that runs without it failed (for example, ten of ten docking-configuration checks, against one to four of ten). By combining automation, reproducibility, and human-in-the-loop control, our Magnolia framework streamlines docking, molecular dynamics and quantum chemistry calculations with direct analysis and LLM-augmented feedback, offering accelerated access to computational (bio)chemistry.

cs.AI / 5 / 2610.27296
Stronger artificial intelligence breakthroughs hasten their own exhaustion
更强大的人工智能突破加速其自身的耗竭
Beichen Lu, Honglin Bao, Qi Huang, Qingguo Meng, James A. Evans
cs.AI · cs.CY · econ.GN
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Progress in artificial intelligence is widely assumed to scale with effort: more researchers, papers and investment should accelerate discovery. Theories of technological growth instead locate the difficulty of discovery in the space of ideas. Here we show that neither scale nor space is enough: breakthroughs depend on diverse attention, which collective concentration can deplete. Across 36 years of computer science, we analyze 7.2 million papers, 73,089 peer reviews and 3.7 million researchers and their topic shifts. The field expanded while its attention narrowed sharply after the Transformer. Over half of topic-shifting researchers moved into AI, especially mid-career ones, and reviewer confidence fell by a full point on a 5-point scale. Each successive breakthrough, from AlexNet to large language models, raised the field's carrying capacity for ideas but was followed by steeper exhaustion of those ideas. Bigger breakthroughs capture attention more completely, depleting the diversity their successors may draw upon. Structural biology shows the same cycle after cryo-EM and AlphaFold. Simulations show how well-intentioned and widely used policies such as reciprocal reviewing empower prolific authors and further narrow what the field accepts. We call for institutions that protect diverse attention in artificial intelligence rather than reward concentration on the winning paradigm.

cs.AI / 6 / 2610.27307
Evolving Self-tuning Benchmarks for Long-Horizon Tool Use
面向长时程工具使用的演化式自调优基准
Hyunji Alex Nam, Michael Dennis, Natasha Jaques, Minsuk Chang
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
For AI assistants to move beyond simple chat interfaces and reliably assist users with applications like Gmail, Venmo, and Slack, we need to improve their tool-use capabilities. However, existing tool use benchmarks are still limited and difficult to scale because they rely on human supervision or are too domain-specific. To make data generation scalable, we propose, TURTLE (**T**ool **U**se **R**elated **T**asks with **L**ong-Horizon **E**volution), an Unsupervised Environment Design (UED) approach to evolve existing tasks using a proposer, a solver, and a feedback generator large language model agents. The proposer is rewarded for difficult yet solvable tasks based on the solver's empirical performance, and the feedback generator summarizes the solver's execution traces for the proposer to exploit. TURTLE produces evolving, self-tuning test suites adaptable to different environment requirements, from supporting user simulators and dense document retrieval to interacting across multiple apps. Empirical results on AppWorld, $τ$-Bench, and AutomationBench using Gemma 4 31B-it show that the evolved tasks target the desired difficulty range (e.g., a 165\% increase in the percentage of hard tasks on AppWorld), increase task diversity (in terms of reasoning and simultaneous tool interactions), and elicit a broader range of failure modes than the original tasks.

cs.AI / 7 / 2610.27347
An LLM-Based Agent for Legal Compliance Assessment: Architecture, Memory, and Evaluation in a Canadian and Quebec Context
基于大语言模型的智能体用于法律合规评估：加拿大与魁北克情境下的架构、记忆与评估
Soukaina Alaoui Ismaili, Jean-Sebastien Dessureault
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Checking whether a text complies with a body of law is slow when done by hand and fragile when done with keyword rules. This paper presents ComplianceAgent, the legal compliance sub-agent of COMPASS, a multi-agent framework that evaluates texts along four axes: digital sovereignty, carbon impact, compliance, and ethics. The agent relies on a large language model that scores a text on a fixed rubric, grounds its judgment in a reference legal corpus, and, when the score falls at or below a critical threshold, runs a corrective chain made of self-healing rewrites, a compliance label, an explainability report, and escalation to a human reviewer. We describe what the language model does at each step, how the memory of the agent is organized, and how the same implementation can be pointed at different reference corpora. We evaluate the agent in a Canadian and Quebec context, on a corpus of thirteen legal instruments that brings together federal and provincial texts, international treaties, and municipal documents of the City of Trois-Rivières. The evaluation relies on a hand-annotated gold standard of fifteen texts and combines classification metrics, a repeated-query stability test, retrieval precision, and a composite score. On this gold standard the agent separates every conforming text from every non-conforming one, its scores remain stable under repeated queries, and the index returns relevant passages.
Chinese Translation
人工检查文本是否遵守某一法律体系时速度缓慢，而使用关键词规则来完成时又十分脆弱。本文介绍 ComplianceAgent，它是 COMPASS 的法律合规子智能体；COMPASS 是一个多智能体框架，沿四个维度评估文本：数字主权、碳影响、合规性和伦理。该智能体依赖一个大语言模型，该模型依据固定评分量表对文本打分，将其判断建立在参考法律语料库之上，并且当分数达到或低于关键阈值时，运行由自愈式重写、合规标签、可解释性报告以及升级至人工审核员组成的纠正链。我们描述该语言模型在每个步骤中做什么、该智能体的记忆如何组织，以及同一实现如何能够指向不同的参考语料库。我们在加拿大与魁北克情境下评估该智能体，所用语料库包含十三项法律文书，汇集了联邦与省级文本、国际条约以及三河市（City of Trois-Rivières）的市政文件。该评估依赖于由十五篇文本组成的人工标注金标准，并结合分类指标、重复查询稳定性测试、检索精确率和综合得分。在该金标准上，该智能体将每一个合规文本与每一个不合规文本区分开来，其分数在重复查询下保持稳定，并且索引返回相关段落。

cs.AI / 8 / 2610.27377
REM: What to Store, When to Recall, What to Forget in Experience Memory for Coding Agents
REM：面向编程智能体的经验记忆——存储什么、何时召回、遗忘什么
Xinyi Lisa Chen, Pedro Herrero-Vidal, Xiaohan Chen, Xiaojing Yu, Cris Liu, Bingqing Song, Bin Xu, Suleiman A. Khan, You-Lin Chen
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language model (LLM) agents now autonomously complete long-horizon tasks, such as repository-level coding, through hundreds of think-act steps, yet the experience each run produces is rarely reused on the next. Prior memory systems concentrate on retrieval, finding the most relevant past trajectory. Retrieval cannot observe the running agent, so it cannot decide whether the agent needs an experience, at which point, or for how long. We introduce REM (Reusable Experience Memory), a framework that manages the memory lifecycle from inside the agent's think-act loop through three explicit decisions. What to store: each completed trajectory is consolidated into a phase-structured document, two orders of magnitude smaller than the trajectory. When to recall: the document is injected at the start of the task; the costlier implementation record is withheld until an in-loop gate detects the agent struggling. What to forget: the record is evicted after a single exposure. On repository-level bug fixing (SWE-ContextBench Lite), REM retrieves the related trajectory more accurately than every state-of-the-art memory system (68.7% vs. 55.6% match@1) and improves, in every replicate, end-task resolution (27.6% vs. 24.9%) at 17% lower cost. Injecting the same experience as a summary or raw trajectory, even when oracle-retrieved, does not. Ablating any of the three decisions reduces resolution. Altogether, these results demonstrate that the bottleneck in experience reuse is not retrieval fidelity but how experience is stored and governed across its lifecycle, opening a control-theoretic perspective on agent memory.

ProMemAgent: Long-Horizon Proactive Assistance with Context-Aware Prospective Memory from Sensory Perceptions
ProMemAgent：基于感官感知的上下文感知前瞻记忆的长时程主动辅助
Lilin Xu, Linyang He, Kaiyuan Hou, Yuang Fan, Minghui Zhao, Xuhai Xu, Xiaofan Jiang
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language model (LLM) agents are moving beyond reactive responses toward proactive assistance that anticipates user needs without explicit requests. However, existing proactive agents primarily address immediate needs, while many everyday situations involve delayed intentions that can only be acted on hours or days later. Humans handle such intentions through prospective memory, the ability to remember to act on an intention when the right moment arises. In this paper, we introduce ProMemAgent, the first proactive agent to incorporate prospective memory over everyday sensory contexts for long-horizon proactive assistance. ProMemAgent organizes past sensory perceptions (e.g., egocentric video and audio) into context-aware memory, generating prospective cues and linking earlier events with subsequent developments for future retrieval. Given the current context, it retrieves relevant past events and performs memory-augmented proactive reasoning to determine whether assistance is needed. We further introduce CPMBench, the first benchmark for evaluating long-horizon proactive assistance over sensory contexts, comprising 1,000 instances across eight everyday categories. Extensive experiments show that ProMemAgent achieves the best memory retrieval performance and consistently outperforms all baselines on long-horizon proactive assistance.

The More the Better? A Comparison of Single- and Multi-Agent LLM Setups on a Financial Review Task
越多越好？单智能体与多智能体 LLM 设置在财务审查任务上的比较
Pei Liu
cs.AI · cs.CE
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Practitioner guidance holds that a large language model reviews a document better when the work is divided among agents. We test a narrow form of it in a controlled comparison of single-agent and multi-agent setups on a financial task, reviewing credit assessment memos against requirements. One agent checks six requirements in one call. A team of three on the same model checks the same memo, two requirements each, in the same words, with no roles or later stage. Labels are known for every requirement on 300 synthetic memos, so misses and false alarms are measured separately. Two primary predictions are tested on four models at a Bonferroni-corrected level. Under an instruction to decide each requirement once, the team catches 0.08 to 0.10 more of the defects that carry an explanation on the three models whose single agent misses some, at the corrected level on two. It raises more false alarms on all four, at the corrected level on three. Balanced accuracy, an exploratory measure, changes by 0.02 or less, and the team uses 2.2 to 2.4 times the tokens. Showing each agent the requirements it was not given reduces the added false alarms on the two Claude models, at the corrected level on one. In exploratory comparisons, sampling the single agent three times and flagging on any draw gives higher balanced accuracy than the team on those models, and the team's results depend on the instruction.

When LLMs Manipulate: Measuring Behavioral, Social, and Temporal Effects
当大语言模型实施操纵时：测量行为、社会与时间效应
Sadia Asif, Israel Antonio Rosales Laguan, Shumaila Asif, Haris Khan, Muneeb Asif, Muhammad Zeeshan Karamat
cs.AI · cs.CL · cs.CY · cs.HC · cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language models (LLMs) can influence user trust and decision-making through subtle linguistic cues, yet the behavioral effects of manipulative outputs remain poorly quantified. We introduce a behavioral computing framework for measuring \textit{behavioral vulnerability}, defined as users' susceptibility to manipulative AI responses. Building on DarkPatterns-LLM benchmark, we generate controlled manipulative stimuli using Manipulation Gradient Descent (MGD), targeting biases associated with authority, urgency, and social proof. We analyze participant responses using the Multi-Stakeholder Impact Assessment Network (MSIAN) to model cross-user influence and the Temporal Harm Propagation Model (THPM) to characterize the persistence of behavioral effects over time. In a study involving 120 participants, manipulative framing produced significant changes in trust calibration and compliance ($p < 0.01$), with effects also propagating across social contexts. These findings highlight the need to extend LLM safety evaluation beyond model outputs to measurable behavioral consequences and provide a computational framework for quantifying individual, social, and temporal risks arising from manipulative AI interactions.

The Show-Up Attack: When Subagents Win Over Their Supervisor
露面攻击：当子代理赢得其主管的支持时
Maosen Zhang, Jianshuo Dong, Yutong Zhang, Jie Zhang, Tianwei Zhang, Han Qiu
cs.AI · cs.CR
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Multi-agent systems are increasingly deployed to coordinate multiple large language model (LLM) agents. However, this also creates new attack surfaces: malicious agents may have chances to exploit the coordination. In this paper, we propose and study the \textit{show-up attack}, in which a malicious subagent manipulates the supervisor into involving it in tasks beyond its assigned scope. To evaluate this risk, we propose SUA-Arena, which implements 6 attack strategies and contains 188 test cases. Then, we evaluate 6 frontier LLMs and find that all of them are vulnerable to show-up attacks. For example, GPT-5.6-Sol as a supervisor suffers an ASR of up to 0.93. Mitigation strategies such as prompting and restricted communication fail to reduce the risk consistently. These results show that multi-agent systems need explicit mechanisms for enforcing authority boundaries.

Samhita Bollepally, Takashi Yamauchi, Marissa West
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Empathetic interaction involves two distinguishable capacities: representing another person's emotional state (cognitive empathy) and generating an appropriate response to that state (affective empathy). We apply this distinction to examine how emotion-related information is internally organized, selectively attended to, and carried through response generation in Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct across 10 emotion categories from the EmpatheticDialogues dataset. Layer-wise linear probing revealed a broad middle-layer region of peak emotion-category decodability, with the layer-11 L2 probe achieving 63.6% held-out accuracy against a 10% chance level and a 54.6% TF-IDF lexical baseline. During response generation, emotion-related user tokens received 1.89 times as much attention per token as other utterance tokens, concentrated across layers 10-15. Target-emotion alignment then decreased from a mean cosine similarity of 0.239 for input representations to 0.125 for generated responses, with positive drift in 77% of examples and the largest shifts for angry and furious. Emotion-category representation, attention allocation, and response-level alignment therefore emerge as distinguishable components of model processing that can be analyzed through a functional cognitive-affective empathy framework. These findings provide a foundation for monitoring emotion representations during generation and leveraging models' existing affective structure to support more naturally empathetic responses without relying on external prompting or explicit emotion conditioning.

large language model

Abstract
Multimodal Large Language Models show strong vision-language capabilities, yet their geometry-centric reasoning remains insufficiently understood. Existing mathematical benchmarks typically rely on rasterized figures and cover limited geometric knowledge areas and response formats, making it difficult to assess whether models reason over geometric structures or exploit superficial visual patterns. We introduce TriGeoBench, a geometry-centric multimodal benchmark constructed from Chinese middle- and high-school mathematics examinations. TriGeoBench contains 7,000 question-answer pairs and 12,235 geometric figures with TikZ code, spanning plane geometry, solid geometry, analytic geometry, function, and vector geometry across diverse response formats. Each instance forms a {question-answer pair, image, TikZ} triplet: question-answer pairs are stored in LaTeX, images as RGB figures, and TikZ preserves geometric topology, symbolic annotations, and relational structure. We evaluate representative open- and closed-source MLLMs through image-to-TikZ and multimodal reasoning probes. Results reveal persistent fine-grained structure and image-text alignment challenges. Oracle experiments with human-curated reference TikZ suggest that accurate executable representations provide complementary geometric cues; they do not evaluate an end-to-end conversion pipeline. TriGeoBench offers a testbed for structure-aware mathematical reasoning.

SCODEL: Shared Canonical Ontology Definitions for Food Entity Linking and Ontology-Grounded Recipe Knowledge Graphs

Nuhu Ibrahim, Rishi Ravikumar, Ayuba Dauda, Fuqi Xu, Robert Stevens, Riza Batista-Navarro
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Identifying recipe entities and linking them to ontology concepts is fundamental for semantic recipe understanding. However, food mentions in recipes are often ambiguous, context-dependent, and lexically diverse, making ontology entity linking (EL) challenging. We propose SCODEL, a streamlined, model-agnostic approach based on a central idea: contextual food mentions and ontology concepts that refer to the same entity should learn the same canonical ontology-oriented definition. SCODEL uses these shared definitions as a semantic normalisation layer, providing complementary semantic information to existing EL models without requiring a new linking architecture. We further introduce ReciLinkD, the first benchmark for contextual food ontology entity linking in recipes. Experiments show that SCODEL consistently improves three modular EL models (ReFinED, GSM-EL, and BLINK): SCODEL x BLINK achieves the highest Hit@1 on seen concepts (88.33%), while SCODEL x GSM-EL achieves the highest Hit@1 on unseen concepts (83.15%), outperforming the strongest large language model (LLM) based EL baseline in each setting. Experiments on a biomedical ontology benchmark further demonstrate that SCODEL generalises beyond the food domain. Finally, we use SCODEL to ground food mentions at scale and construct an ontology-grounded recipe knowledge graph, demonstrating its utility for ontology-aware recipe retrieval and corpus-level food analysis.

When Can LLM Reasoning Reliably Reuse Intermediate Results?

large language model

Abstract
Sampling complete solutions gives large language models more chances to solve a problem, but each attempt starts again. For tasks with several subproblems, all required answers must be correct in the same attempt. Retaining intermediate results can avoid repeating correct work, but errors in those results may affect later attempts. We study when this reuse is reliable and how much computation it requires. For local retries that stop when no candidate passes within the retry budget, we give conditions for correct completion and bound the average number of attempts. We also show how checking cost and the chance of passing a check affect total computation. Experiments across eight reasoning models examine composite mathematics and arithmetic. Across four DeepSeek models, average success on the second subproblem is 36.2 percent without first-subproblem context, 57.2 percent with its answer, and 58.3 percent with its reasoning and answer. These scores measure second-subproblem coverage and include continuations made when selection fails. Arithmetic experiments show that similar first-attempt accuracies can lead to very different coverage after repeated attempts. Code is available at https://github.com/SempraETY/Intermediate-State-Reuse.

Pattern Intelligence: Unsupervised, LLM-Interpreted Discovery of Systematic Underpayment and Denial Patterns in Healthcare Revenue Cycle Management
Pattern Intelligence：医疗收入周期管理中系统性少付与拒付模式的无监督、LLM 解释发现
Harshil Lodhiya, Alex McManus
cs.AI · stat.ML
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Healthcare providers lose substantial revenue to systematic payer underpayments and claim denials, yet identifying the recurring, correctable patterns behind them remains largely manual and does not scale to hospital claim volumes. We present Pattern Intelligence, a deployed system that discovers such patterns without supervision by clustering claims on their adjudication behaviour rather than their identity. Each claim is embedded in a 130-dimensional vector combining per-line expected-versus-actual payment ratios, claim adjustment reason (CARC) codes, denial and payment signals, and service composition. Payer and contract identity are deliberately excluded from the distance metric - we show they dominate the geometry and collapse clusters into trivial per-payer groups - and are reintroduced only as a post-hoc segmentation (by contract and visit type) that keeps every surfaced pattern coherent and actionable. We cluster with HDBSCAN, recover structure from the noise set via second-pass sub-clustering, and gate low-confidence memberships. A large language model translates each centroid into an analyst-ready description of dominant procedures, adjustment reasons, and failure mode. We report a recurring finding: roughly one-third to one-half of high-dollar denials, depending on tenant and segmentation, form an irreducible long tail that no density-clustering configuration or representation we tried groups - a domain property, we argue, rather than a modeling deficiency. We evaluate validity through cluster-coherence analysis and quantify impact with a recoverable-opportunity ($) metric on two production tenants (approx. 10K and 157K claims) within a six-tenant deployment. Rather than a new algorithm, the contribution is a problem formulation, a representation-design insight, and empirical findings from production.
Chinese Translation
医疗服务提供者因支付方的系统性少付和索赔拒付而损失大量收入，然而识别其背后反复出现且可纠正的模式在很大程度上仍依赖人工，无法扩展到医院的索赔量规模。我们提出 Pattern Intelligence，这是一个已部署的系统，它通过依据索赔的裁定行为而非其身份对索赔进行聚类，在无监督的情况下发现此类模式。每条索赔被嵌入一个 130 维向量，该向量结合了逐行预期与实际支付比率、索赔调整原因（CARC）代码、拒付和支付信号以及服务构成。支付方和合同身份被有意排除在距离度量之外——我们表明它们主导几何结构，并将聚类坍缩为按支付方划分的平凡分组——仅在事后分割（按合同和就诊类型）中重新引入，以保持每个呈现出的模式连贯且可操作。我们使用 HDBSCAN 进行聚类，通过第二遍子聚类从噪声集中恢复结构，并对低置信度的成员关系进行门控。大语言模型将每个质心转化为可供分析师直接使用的描述，涵盖主要操作、调整原因和失效模式。我们报告一个反复出现的发现：取决于租户和分割方式，大约三分之一到二分之一的高额拒付形成一个不可约的长尾，我们尝试过的任何密度聚类配置或表示都无法将其分组——我们认为这是一种领域属性，而非建模缺陷。我们通过聚类连贯性分析评估有效性，并在一个包含六个租户的部署中，对两个生产租户（约 1 万条和 15.7 万条索赔）使用可回收机会（$）指标量化影响。贡献并非一种新算法，而是一个问题形式化、一个表示设计洞见，以及来自生产环境的实证发现。

cs.AI / 18 / 2610.27699
E8-QAT: Efficient 2-Bit Quantization-Aware Training with Implicit Lattice Codebooks
E8-QAT：基于隐式格码本的高效 2 比特量化感知训练
Xinyu Lei, Hong Huang, Jiebin Zhang, Hongyu Li, Jinlong Song, Decheng Wu, Guanghua Yu, Jianchen Zhu, Sujian Li
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Low-bit quantization reduces the memory footprint of large language models, but preserving accuracy with efficient training remains challenging. Scalar quantization encodes weights independently, while explicit-codebook vector quantization introduces costly search during training. We propose E8-QAT, a 2-bit quantization-aware training framework that uses the $E_8$ lattice as an implicit eight-dimensional codebook. It jointly quantizes weight groups through arithmetic projection without storing or searching an explicit codebook during the training forward pass. A 2-bit core encoding and sparse extension preserve the selected lattice points exactly, adding less than 0.1\% to core index storage. On Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, E8-QAT matches the performance of the full-precision model in terms of the average score across the four tasks. E8-QAT improves over the state-of-the-art baseline by 2.03\% on IFEval and by 1.51\% on LiveCodeBench, under the same data, schedule, and bit width. The 2-bit representation reduces peak memory by 80\% and supports a $4\times$ larger batch. At each representation's largest feasible batch, E8-QAT reaches $1.97\times$ the decoding throughput of BF16.
Chinese Translation
低位量化降低了大语言模型的内存占用，但在高效训练的同时保持精度仍然具有挑战性。标量量化独立地编码权重，而显式码本向量量化在训练过程中引入了昂贵的搜索。我们提出 E8-QAT，一个 2 比特量化感知训练框架，它使用 $E_8$ 格作为隐式的八维码本。它通过算术投影对权重分组进行联合量化，在训练前向传播过程中无需存储或搜索显式码本。2 比特核心编码与稀疏扩展精确地保留了所选的格点，仅使核心索引存储增加不到 0.1\%。在 Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 上，E8-QAT 在四项任务的平均得分方面与全精度模型的性能相当。在相同的数据、训练计划和比特宽度下，E8-QAT 在 IFEval 上比最先进的基线提升了 2.03\%，在 LiveCodeBench 上提升了 1.51\%。2 比特表示将峰值内存降低 80\%，并支持 $4\times$ 更大的批次。在每种表示各自的最大可行批次下，E8-QAT 的解码吞吐量达到 BF16 的 $1.97\times$。

cs.AI / 19 / 2610.27847
SAPD: Learning from Agent Experience without Environment Interaction
SAPD：无需环境交互地从智能体经验中学习
Juncheng Diao, Haibin Wang, Wei Shi, Yifan Ding, Qingbin Li, Rongxiang Weng, Xunliang Cai
cs.AI · cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Scaling the training of Large Language Model (LLM) agents typically requires a large collection of executable environments, whose construction, maintenance, and operation constrain the expansion of training experience. Existing offline trajectories offer an opportunity to reuse interaction experience, yet effectively refining the current policy without revisiting these environments remains challenging: supervised fine-tuning (SFT) can lead to catastrophic forgetting, while online reinforcement learning requires real-time interaction with the environment. To address this challenge, we propose Step-Advantage Policy Distillation (SAPD), a method for learning from offline trajectories using relative step advantages. SAPD decomposes multi-turn trajectories into individual decision contexts for on-policy distillation, allowing the student to generate responses conditioned on recorded histories, and introduces relative step advantage signals to stabilize training. The entire process requires neither new environment observations nor additional multi-turn interactions. Experiments on ALFWorld, WebShop, and Search-based QA show that SAPD improves performance across different teacher configurations, mitigates catastrophic forgetting compared with SFT, and runs at least $4.7\times$ faster per training step than online OPD. We will release our code soon.
Chinese Translation
扩展大型语言模型（LLM）智能体的训练通常需要大量可执行环境，而这些环境的构建、维护和运行制约了训练经验的扩展。现有的离线轨迹为复用交互经验提供了机会，然而在不重新访问这些环境的情况下有效改进当前策略仍然具有挑战性：监督微调（SFT）可能导致灾难性遗忘，而在线强化学习需要与环境的实时交互。为应对这一挑战，我们提出步级优势策略蒸馏（Step-Advantage Policy Distillation，SAPD），一种利用相对步级优势从离线轨迹中学习的方法。SAPD 将多轮轨迹分解为单个决策上下文以进行同策略蒸馏，使学生模型能够以记录的历史为条件生成响应，并引入相对步级优势信号以稳定训练。整个过程既不需要新的环境观测，也不需要额外的多轮交互。在 ALFWorld、WebShop 和基于搜索的问答任务上的实验表明，SAPD 在不同的教师配置下均能提升性能，与 SFT 相比缓解了灾难性遗忘，并且每个训练步骤的运行速度至少比在线 OPD 快 $4.7\times$。我们将很快发布代码。

cs.AI / 20 / 2610.27913
ACE-Compression: An Ability-Centric Evaluation of Compressed Large Language Models
ACE-Compression：一种以能力为中心的压缩大语言模型评估方法
Jiahui Ning, Liang Chen, Yuchen Liang, Yi Zhang, Fenglei Fan
cs.AI · cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Model compression makes large language models deployable, but today's evaluation tells an incomplete story. Standard practice measures retained task performance and stops there. This misses a critical fact: compression perturbs the distributed knowledge embedded across billions of weights, and task scores alone cannot reveal which underlying abilities survive and which quietly collapse. To solve this question, we introduce ACE-Compression, an ability-centric evaluation framework. Instead of asking only "does the compressed model still answer correctly?", we ask "which of its core abilities remain intact?" Our framework probes four deployment-facing dimensions: procedural reasoning and constraint execution, knowledge grounding and truthfulness, social cognition and affective understanding, and persona fidelity and stylistic consistency. Across more than 35 compressed checkpoints from six open-weight LLMs-covering quantization and pruning-we find that compression redistributes ability profiles. Coarse, local, and surface-level signals often persist, while fine-grained, long-tail, and context-dependent abilities become fragile. Quantization consistently outperforms pruning in retention, but the practical meaning of that gap depends entirely on which ability an application requires. Based on our findings, deployers can choose compression methods by the ability profile their application needs, not just by a leaderboard average. And algorithm designers gain diagnostic signals to build compression methods that preserve what matters. We believe that ACE-Compression turns compression from a black-box accuracy drop into an interpretable intervention-one we can measure, understand, and ultimately improve.
Chinese Translation
模型压缩使大语言模型得以部署，但当今的评估却只讲述了不完整的故事。标准做法是测量保留下来的任务性能，然后就到此为止。这忽略了一个关键事实：压缩会扰动嵌入在数十亿权重之中的分布式知识，而仅凭任务分数无法揭示哪些底层能力得以存活、哪些能力悄然崩塌。为解决这一问题，我们提出 ACE-Compression，一个以能力为中心的评估框架。我们不再只问“压缩后的模型是否仍能正确作答？”，而是问“它的哪些核心能力仍然完好无损？”我们的框架探测四个面向部署的维度：程序性推理与约束执行、知识依据与真实性、社会认知与情感理解，以及人格保真度与风格一致性。在来自六个开放权重大语言模型的 35 个以上压缩检查点上——涵盖量化与剪枝——我们发现压缩会重新分布能力画像。粗粒度、局部和表层信号往往得以保留，而细粒度、长尾和依赖上下文的能力则变得脆弱。在保持率上，量化始终优于剪枝，但这一差距的实际意义完全取决于应用需要哪一种能力。基于我们的发现，部署者可以根据其应用所需的能力画像来选择压缩方法，而不仅仅依据排行榜上的平均分。算法设计者则获得了诊断信号，用以构建能够保留关键要素的压缩方法。我们相信，ACE-Compression 将压缩从一种黑箱式的精度下降转变为一种可解释的干预——一种我们可以测量、理解并最终改进的干预。

cs.AI / 21 / 2610.28003
Dancing Diffusion: Learning Continuous Programs for Image Generation and Editing
Dancing Diffusion：学习用于图像生成与编辑的连续程序
Cui Enhe, Jinyue Yang, Bojian Yin, Guoqi Li
cs.AI · cs.GR
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Diffusion models generate samples through a multi-step denoising trajectory, yet condition every step on the same instruction, so the trajectory cannot be addressed at the level of individual operations. We introduce Dancing Diffusion, which assigns each span of timesteps a dedicated continuous condition block and thereby turns conditioning into a latent program. A compiler maps text features into this program, and a fixed pretrained generator executes its blocks over successive sampling intervals. The trajectory can then dance, keeping its executed history while its continuation is redirected. A shared prefix is executed once and reused, and a later operation is rewritten while content fixed by earlier operations is preserved. The compiler is trained through the images it produces, with visual feedback on both the requested change and the retained content. On SANA, reusing an executed prefix preserves markedly more of the scene than regenerating from noise at a similar strength of edit, learned conditions preserve more background than native prompt switching from the same saved state, and the learned program improves generation quality over native SANA. Later branches weaken the edit, which leaves semantic control over individual operations limited. By converting a single-instruction trajectory into a program of addressable operations, Dancing Diffusion lays a foundation for structured intermediate computation in diffusion models.
Chinese Translation
扩散模型通过多步去噪轨迹生成样本，但每一步都以相同的指令为条件，因此无法在单个操作的层面上对轨迹进行寻址。我们提出 Dancing Diffusion，它为每一段时间步分配一个专用的连续条件块，从而将条件化转变为潜在程序。编译器将文本特征映射到该程序中，固定的预训练生成器在相继的采样区间内执行其各个块。轨迹于是可以“舞动”，在保留已执行历史的同时重定向其后续部分。共享前缀执行一次并被复用，后续操作被重写，同时由先前操作固定的内容得以保留。编译器通过其生成的图像进行训练，并获得关于所请求更改和所保留内容的视觉反馈。在 SANA 上，复用已执行的前缀比在相近编辑强度下从噪声重新生成能显著保留更多场景，学习到的条件比从同一保存状态进行原生提示切换保留更多背景，且学习到的程序相比原生 SANA 提升了生成质量。后续分支会削弱编辑，这使得对单个操作的语义控制仍然有限。通过将单指令轨迹转换为由可寻址操作组成的程序，Dancing Diffusion 为扩散模型中的结构化中间计算奠定了基础。

cs.AI / 22 / 2610.28060
TrajEvolve: Trajectory Evolution for Reinforcement Learning with Hindsight Credit Assignment
TrajEvolve：面向后见信用分配强化学习的轨迹进化
Yi Wen, Hao Chen, Wanyu Wang, Maolin Wang, Pengyue Jia, Derong Xu, Huize Tan, Yingyi Zhang, Wenlin Zhang, Weihong Luo, Xiku Du, Xiangyu Zhao
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
The Reinforcement Learning (RL) paradigm has achieved remarkable success in enhancing the reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs). However, when applied to long-horizon tasks, it faces severe challenges: i) Due to the high task complexity, the model struggles to sample enough successful trajectories, resulting in slow convergence. ii) Relying solely on sparse final rewards causes all steps to be updated indiscriminately, encouraging redundant step generation. When both the quantity and quality of successful trajectories become difficult to guarantee, the performance is severely constrained. This dilemma stems from the limitations: existing RL paradigms rely entirely on the reasoning capability of base models, lacking the ability to actively optimize trajectories. To address the above issues, we propose a novel trajectory evolution paradigm with hindsight credit assignment, termed TrajEvolve. TrajEvolve not only relies on the trajectory inferred by the model but also generates ``evolutionary trajectories'' by refining low-quality steps in historical trajectories, thereby exposing the policy to high-quality compositions that lie within the base model's support but are rarely sampled within practical training budgets. Furthermore, TrajEvolve reformulates step-level continuous credit assignment as a binary classification task, whether each step is necessary for task completion. This simplification not only reduces the learning difficulty but also enables step labels to be obtained through counterfactual verification, achieving precise identification of redundant steps. Extensive experiments on two datasets demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method.
Chinese Translation
强化学习（RL）范式在增强大语言模型（LLMs）的推理能力方面取得了显著成功。然而，当应用于长时程任务时，它面临严峻挑战：i) 由于任务复杂度高，模型难以采样到足够多的成功轨迹，导致收敛缓慢。ii) 仅依赖稀疏的最终奖励会导致所有步骤被不加区分地更新，从而鼓励冗余步骤的生成。当成功轨迹的数量和质量都难以保证时，性能会受到严重制约。这一困境源于以下局限：现有的RL范式完全依赖基座模型的推理能力，缺乏主动优化轨迹的能力。为解决上述问题，我们提出了一种具有后见信用分配的新型轨迹进化范式，称为TrajEvolve。TrajEvolve不仅依赖模型推断出的轨迹，还通过精炼历史轨迹中的低质量步骤来生成“进化轨迹”，从而使策略接触到高质量组合，这些组合位于基座模型的支持范围内，但在实际训练预算内很少被采样。此外，TrajEvolve将步骤级连续信用分配重新表述为一个二分类任务，即每个步骤对于任务完成是否必要。这种简化不仅降低了学习难度，还使得步骤标签能够通过反事实验证获得，从而实现对冗余步骤的精确识别。在两个数据集上的大量实验证明了所提方法的优越性。

cs.AI / 23 / 2610.28201
MaD-RSI: Model-as-Data for Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Harnesses
MaD-RSI：模型即数据，用于智能体执行框架的递归自我改进
Yu Cui, Hong He, Ruiqing Yue, Sicheng Pan, Zhuoyu Sun, Yifei Liu, Ting Li, Wenzhuo Zhu, Baohan Huang, Haibin Zhang, Cong Zuo
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Recursive self-improvement (RSI) of agent harnesses has emerged as an effective approach to enhancing the capabilities of large language model (LLM) agents. By searching the harness space for a specific LLM on a given dataset, RSI can discover a harness tailored to the capabilities and behavioral characteristics of that model. However, such optimization often creates a strong coupling between the learned harness and its target LLM, limiting generalization across models and requiring substantial computational resources to adapt to new LLMs. Moreover, existing RSI methods typically optimize a harness using feedback from a single model and evaluate its generalization to other models only after training. This paradigm treats model differences primarily as a criterion for evaluating generalization rather than as valuable evidence for optimization. In this paper, we introduce a new perspective that treats models as data and places the harness at the center of optimization. Building on this perspective, we propose \textsc{MaD-RSI}, a framework that directly optimizes a shared harness across multiple heterogeneous LLMs by incorporating their diverse failure trajectories into the training process. Rather than assessing model differences only after optimization, \textsc{MaD-RSI} leverages these differences as training evidence to guide the self-improvement of a shared harness. Furthermore, we introduce a new evaluation framework with two complementary metrics designed to assess the effectiveness of harness optimization across models. Experiments across multiple datasets and LLMs demonstrate that \textsc{MaD-RSI} improves generalization over existing approaches while reducing training costs.
Chinese Translation
智能体执行框架的递归自我改进（RSI）已成为提升大语言模型（LLM）智能体能力的一种有效方法。通过在给定数据集上为特定 LLM 搜索执行框架空间，RSI 能够发现一个适应该模型能力和行为特征的执行框架。然而，这种优化通常会在所学习到的执行框架与其目标 LLM 之间产生强耦合，限制了跨模型的泛化，并且需要大量计算资源才能适配新的 LLM。此外，现有的 RSI 方法通常利用来自单一模型的反馈来优化执行框架，并且仅在训练之后才评估其对其他模型的泛化能力。这种范式主要将模型差异视为评估泛化能力的标准，而不是将其视为有价值的优化证据。在本文中，我们引入一种新视角，即将模型视为数据，并将执行框架置于优化的中心。基于这一视角，我们提出 \textsc{MaD-RSI}，该框架通过将多个异构 LLM 的多样化失败轨迹纳入训练过程，直接跨多个异构 LLM 优化一个共享执行框架。\textsc{MaD-RSI} 不在优化之后才评估模型差异，而是将这些差异作为训练证据，以指导共享执行框架的自我改进。此外，我们引入一个新的评估框架，其中包含两个互补指标，旨在评估执行框架优化在跨模型情形下的有效性。在多个数据集和 LLM 上的实验表明，\textsc{MaD-RSI} 在降低训练成本的同时，相较现有方法提升了泛化能力。

cs.AI / 24 / 2610.28282
ChartEvo: Self-Evolving Agent Harnesses for Long-Tail Chart Reasoning
ChartEvo：面向长尾图表推理的自进化智能体执行框架
Qi Wang, Peijie Wang, Jun Cao, Haoyang Tong, Xiao-Hui Li, Fei Yin, Cheng-Lin Liu
cs.AI · cs.CV
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have substantially advanced chart understanding and reasoning, yet their performance remains highly uneven across chart types. While modern MLLMs perform well on common charts, their accuracy drops sharply on long-tail charts with diverse visual structures and reasoning requirements. Tool-augmented agents can improve complex chart reasoning by introducing specialized visual capabilities, but manually engineering strategies and tools for the heterogeneous and evolving long tail is difficult to scale. We introduce \textbf{ChartEvo}, a recursive self-improvement framework that enables chart agents to adapt to underperforming chart types through experience-driven harness-level self-improvement. ChartEvo jointly evolves reusable chart-specific Skills and executable Tools, while learning reusable local tool-call chains to compose evolved capabilities and control the inference overhead of tool-augmented reasoning. On long-tail charts from ChartBench and ChartX, ChartEvo improves accuracy over its base MLLM, Qwen3.7-Plus, by \textbf{45.6\%} and \textbf{32.5\%}, respectively, demonstrating the effectiveness of recursive self-improvement for long-tail chart adaptation.
Chinese Translation
多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）已显著推进图表理解与推理，但其在不同图表类型上的性能仍高度不均衡。尽管现代 MLLMs 在常见图表上表现良好，但在具有多样视觉结构和推理需求的长尾图表上，其准确率会急剧下降。工具增强的智能体可以通过引入专门的视觉能力来改进复杂图表推理，但为异构且不断演进的长尾手动设计策略和工具难以扩展。我们提出 \textbf{ChartEvo}，一个递归式自我改进框架，使图表智能体能够通过经验驱动的执行框架层面自我改进来适应表现不佳的图表类型。ChartEvo 联合演化可复用的图表专用技能（Skills）和可执行工具（Tools），同时学习可复用的局部工具调用链，以组合演化出的能力并控制工具增强推理的推理开销。在来自 ChartBench 和 ChartX 的长尾图表上，ChartEvo 相较于其基础 MLLM——Qwen3.7-Plus——分别将准确率提升了 \textbf{45.6\%} 和 \textbf{32.5\%}，证明了递归式自我改进在长尾图表适应方面的有效性。

cs.AI / 25 / 2610.28405
DIVE: Benchmarking Full-Duplex Interaction with Visual Engagement in Continuous Streams
DIVE：在连续流中基准测试具有视觉参与的全双工交互
Yuhang Chen, Guangyue Liu, Shilong Liu
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Recent advances in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have substantially improved spoken interaction and video understanding. Existing online and streaming benchmarks primarily assess causal multimodal perception through timestamped question answering, whereas real-world interaction requires models to continuously identify task-relevant multimodal cues and decide whether, when, and how to respond. This leaves open how well current models can sustain real-time interaction throughout an evolving multimodal stream. To address this gap, we introduce DIVE, a benchmark for evaluating full-duplex interaction with visual engagement under continuous and realistic multimodal streams. It organizes six tasks into three complementary interaction scenarios. (1) Proactive Intervention evaluates whether models can identify emerging visual or semantic cues and intervene at the appropriate moment. (2) Continuous Engagement evaluates sustained participation through continuous visual tracking and visually grounded query interaction. (3) Interaction Coordination evaluates how models coordinate listening and speaking under overlapping and multi-party interactions. DIVE contains 525 audio/video samples with fine-grained human annotations and precise temporal metadata. Its evaluation protocol separates response quality, participation decisions, and response timing. We evaluate representative real-time models using response quality, window response rates, and reaction latency. Experiments show that leading real-time models achieve sub-second average response latency, yet their average window response rates remain at or below 53.77%. Response quality varies substantially across models and tasks, with adapting ongoing responses to newly arriving information remaining particularly challenging. We hope DIVE facilitates progress toward more natural and capable real-time multimodal interactive systems.

近期多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）的进展显著提升了语音交互与视频理解。现有的在线与流式基准主要通过带时间戳的问答来评估因果多模态感知，而真实世界交互要求模型持续识别与任务相关的多模态线索，并决定是否回应、何时回应以及如何回应。这使得当前模型能否在持续演变的多模态流中维持实时交互这一问题仍未得到解答。为弥补这一空白，我们提出 DIVE，一个用于评估在连续且真实的多模态流下具有视觉参与的全双工交互的基准。它将六个任务组织为三个互补的交互场景。（1）主动干预（Proactive Intervention）评估模型能否识别新出现的视觉或语义线索，并在适当时机进行干预。（2）持续参与（Continuous Engagement）通过持续视觉跟踪和基于视觉的查询交互来评估持续参与。（3）交互协调（Interaction Coordination）评估模型在重叠和多方可交互中如何协调听与说。DIVE 包含 525 个音视频样本，配有细粒度人工标注和精确的时间元数据。其评估协议将回复质量、参与决策和回复时机分开评估。我们使用回复质量、窗口响应率和反应延迟来评估具有代表性的实时模型。实验表明，领先的实时模型实现了亚秒级平均响应延迟，但其平均窗口响应率仍处于或低于 53.77%。回复质量在不同模型和任务之间差异显著，而将进行中的回复适应新到达的信息仍然尤其具有挑战性。我们希望 DIVE 能促进朝着更自然、更有能力的实时多模态交互系统取得进展。

cs.AI / 26 / 2610.28441
Stratified Sparse Attention: Reducing the Sparse-to-Dense Gap at Extreme Sparsity
分层稀疏注意力：在极端稀疏性下缩小稀疏到稠密的差距
Sahil Joshi, Prithvi Dixit, Aryan Katiyar, Agniva Chowdhury, Joseph E. Gonzalez, Anshumali Shrivastava, Aditya Desai, Kumar Krishna Agrawal
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large Language Model inference over long contexts is increasingly bottlenecked by the cost of attending to a growing Key-Value (KV) cache. Sparse attention reduces this cost by accessing only a fraction of the cache, but existing methods face a trade-off between deterministic retrieval, which captures high-scoring tokens but discards residual attention mass, and sampling, which improves coverage at the cost of higher variance. Hybrid methods combine top-$k$ retrieval with uniform sampling, yet still exhibit a substantial gap from dense attention at aggressive sparsity. We introduce \emph{Stratified Sparse Attention (SSA)}, a unified framework combining deterministic retrieval with score-guided sampling. SSA deterministically attends to high-scoring tokens while sampling the residual using proxy attention scores and correcting for their inclusion probabilities, thereby recovering attention mass beyond the retrieval set. SSA encompasses top-$k$, top-$p$, and hybrid top-$k$+sampling as special cases. Across RULER, LongBench, LOFT, and AIME, and five models ranging from 3B to 27B parameters, SSA consistently improves over the baselines at matched sparsity. On RULER-HARD with Ministral-3-8B, SSA improves accuracy over the strongest practical baseline from 81.8\% to 84.2\% at 32K and from 63.8\% to 69.3\% at 128K under $50\times$ attention sparsity, recovering 94\% and 85\% of dense-attention performance, respectively. With optimized CUDA kernels, SSA achieves up to $2.96\times$ decode speedup over FlashInfer at 1M context, demonstrating that its accuracy gains translate into practical long-context inference acceleration. We open-source our code at https://github.com/skylight-org/SSA-Paper-Code.
Chinese Translation
长上下文中的大语言模型推理日益受限于对不断增长的键值（KV）缓存执行注意力计算的开销。稀疏注意力通过仅访问缓存的一小部分来降低这一成本，但现有方法面临一种权衡：确定性检索能够捕获高分 token，却会丢弃残余注意力质量；而采样则以更高方差为代价提高覆盖率。混合方法将 top-$k$ 检索与均匀采样相结合，但在激进稀疏度下仍与稠密注意力存在显著差距。我们提出分层稀疏注意力（Stratified Sparse Attention, SSA），这是一个将确定性检索与分数引导采样相结合的统一框架。SSA 确定性地关注高分 token，同时使用代理注意力分数对残余部分进行采样，并校正其包含概率，从而恢复检索集之外的注意力质量。SSA 将 top-$k$、top-$p$ 以及混合 top-$k$+采样作为特例囊括其中。在 RULER、LongBench、LOFT 和 AIME 上，以及在从 3B 到 27B 参数的五个模型上，SSA 在匹配稀疏度下始终优于基线。在 Ministral-3-8B 上的 RULER-HARD 中，在 $50\times$ 注意力稀疏度下，SSA 将准确率相对于最强实用基线在 32K 时从 81.8% 提升到 84.2%，在 128K 时从 63.8% 提升到 69.3%，分别恢复稠密注意力性能的 94% 和 85%。借助优化的 CUDA 内核，SSA 在 1M 上下文下相较 FlashInfer 实现最高 $2.96\times$ 的解码加速，表明其准确率提升可转化为实际的长上下文推理加速。我们在 https://github.com/skylight-org/SSA-Paper-Code 开源了代码。

Beyond the Sequentiality Bottleneck: A Hybrid Diffusion-Autoregressive Framework for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning
超越序列性瓶颈：面向高效多模态推理的混合扩散-自回归框架
Wei Cai, Jian Zhao, Yuchen Yuan, Xuelong Li
cs.AI
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Autoregressive models (ARMs) face a "Sequentiality Bottleneck" in reasoning, while diffusion language models (DLMs) offer parallelism but lack semantic coherence. To addresses both limitations, we propose Collaborative Reasoning Asymmetric Learning (CoRAL), a hybrid framework via an Asymmetric Planner-Executor (APE) architecture: a DLM Planner generates K diverse reasoning trajectories in parallel, while a large ARM Executor selects the optimal plan and synthesizes the final answer. To train the Planner effectively, we introduce Reward-Guided Denoising for CoT (RDC), which integrates outcome-based rewards into the diffusion process to steer it toward goal-directed reasoning. Experiments on vision-language benchmarks show that CoRAL significantly outperforms prior diffusion-based methods and achieves competitive performance against strong ARMs, achieving both superior efficiency and quality.

自回归模型（ARMs）在推理中面临“序列性瓶颈”，而扩散语言模型（DLMs）虽提供并行性，却缺乏语义连贯性。为解决这两个局限，我们提出协作推理非对称学习（CoRAL），这是一种通过非对称规划器-执行器（APE）架构实现的混合框架：DLM 规划器并行生成 K 条多样化的推理轨迹，而大型 ARM 执行器选择最优计划并合成最终答案。为有效训练规划器，我们引入面向思维链的奖励引导去噪（RDC），它将基于结果的奖励整合到扩散过程中，以引导其朝向目标导向的推理。在视觉-语言基准上的实验表明，CoRAL 显著优于先前的基于扩散的方法，并在与强 ARM 的对比中取得有竞争力的性能，同时实现了更优的效率和质量。

Value-Rich, Differently Organized: Measuring Value Expression and Organization in AI-Generated Debates
价值丰富，组织方式不同：测量AI生成辩论中的价值表达与组织
Maoyuan Li, Haoyuan Li, Zhongsheng Wang, Jiamou Liu
cs.AI
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Current evaluation of LLM-generated debate largely focuses on argumentative quality, leaving the value structure of generated arguments underexamined. We introduce a diagnostic metric framework for comparing how values are expressed and organized in human-reference and AI-generated debates. The framework separates value expression, the range of recognizable values a debate invokes, from value organization, how those values are distributed and sustained across turns. Grounded in Schwartz's Basic-10 value theory, it represents debates as multi-level value distributions over argumentative units, utterances, stances, and full debates, enabling metrics for value coverage, alignment, diffusion, and cross-turn dynamics. Across multiple generation systems, AI-generated debates are broadly value-expressive, often activating as many or more value dimensions than matched human references, but they organize these values differently. Their utterances are more locally value-diffuse, and source-blind judges distinguish value clarity from value focus. These findings show that debate evaluation should consider not only value presence, but also value organization. Code and supplementary materials are available at https://github.com/Maoyuan-li/Value-Expression-and-Organization.

当前对LLM生成辩论的评估主要集中于论证质量，而生成论证的价值结构仍未得到充分考察。我们引入一个诊断性指标框架，用于比较人类参考辩论与AI生成辩论中价值如何被表达和组织。该框架将价值表达（一场辩论所援引的可识别价值的范围）与价值组织（这些价值如何在各个轮次中分布和维持）区分开来。该框架以Schwartz的基本10种价值理论为基础，将辩论表示为在论证单元、话语、立场和完整辩论上的多层次价值分布，从而能够构建价值覆盖度、对齐度、扩散度和跨轮次动态的指标。在多个生成系统中，AI生成的辩论广泛具有价值表达性，常常激活与匹配的人类参考一样多或更多的价值维度，但它们以不同方式组织这些价值。它们的话语在局部上具有更高的价值扩散性，而来源盲判者能够区分价值清晰度与价值聚焦度。这些发现表明，辩论评估不仅应考虑价值是否存在，还应考虑价值组织。代码和补充材料可在 https://github.com/Maoyuan-li/Value-Expression-and-Organization 获取。

cs.AI / 29 / 2610.28611
Semantic Observability for Autonomous Systems Diagnostics
面向自主系统诊断的语义可观测性
Jitendra Solanki, Anand Todkar, Ziran Min
cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Modern distributed microservice deployments generate massive volumes of heterogeneous, multi-format observability logs across physically and logically partitioned infrastructure. Isolating root causes during cascading failures remains an arduous task for Site Reliability Engineers (SREs), bottlenecked by manual keyword filtering and disjointed temporal correlation across monitoring dashboards. We introduce Semantic Observability, an autonomous multi-agent framework that unifies disparate log streams into a dynamic, queryable Property Graph Database. By modeling physical infrastructure topologies, logical software dependencies, and chronological event sequences as attributed nodes and directed relations, it bridges the semantic gap inherent in flat, unstructured log repositories. Building on this unified substrate, we deploy a stateful multi-agent system orchestrated through Directed Cyclic Graphs (DCGs). The system autonomously navigates the topology, applying causal graph algorithms and temporal back-traversal to isolate the precise blast radius of anomalies. The pruned subgraph is then interpreted by a Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning engine to generate contextualized, code-level Root Cause Analyses (RCA) and actionable remediations. This paper establishes the foundational system architecture, formal relational ontology, and multi-agent control loops of Semantic Observability. We show conceptually how the framework eliminates ambient telemetry noise, reduces Mean Time to Resolution (MTTR), compresses LLM token consumption, and prevents structural hallucinations. We also specify an open-source validation framework on standard benchmarks (LogHub and Train-Ticket), laying the groundwork for a forthcoming companion paper on exhaustive quantitative evaluation and production benchmarking.

现代分布式微服务部署会在物理和逻辑分区的基础设施上生成海量异构、多格式的可观测性日志。在级联故障期间定位根因对于站点可靠性工程师（SRE）而言仍是一项艰巨任务，受制于人工关键词过滤以及跨监控仪表盘的割裂式时间关联。我们提出语义可观测性（Semantic Observability），一个自主多智能体框架，它将分散的日志流统一为一个动态、可查询的属性图数据库。通过将物理基础设施拓扑、逻辑软件依赖关系和时间顺序事件序列建模为带属性的节点和有向关系，它弥合了扁平、非结构化日志存储库中固有的语义鸿沟。在此统一基座之上，我们部署了一个通过有向循环图（DCG）编排的有状态多智能体系统。该系统自主导航拓扑结构，应用因果图算法和时间反向遍历来隔离异常的精确爆炸半径。随后，经剪枝的子图由大语言模型（LLM）推理引擎解释，以生成情境化的、代码级的根因分析（RCA）和可操作的修复措施。本文建立了语义可观测性的基础系统架构、形式化关系本体和多智能体控制回路。我们从概念上说明该框架如何消除环境遥测噪声、降低平均解决时间（MTTR）、压缩 LLM token 消耗并防止结构性幻觉。我们还规定了在标准基准（LogHub 和 Train-Ticket）上的开源验证框架，为后续关于详尽定量评估和生产基准测试的姊妹论文奠定基础。

A Bochner Weitzenböck Decomposition for Cellular Sheaf Laplacians, Curvature and Neural Sheaf Diffusion
胞腔层拉普拉斯算子的 Bochner-Weitzenböck 分解、曲率与神经层扩散
Francesco Maria Guadagnuolo, Alessio Borgi, Dorina Thanou, Pietro Liò
cs.CG · cs.LG
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
We extend the Bochner-Weitzenböck decomposition to cellular sheaf Laplacians, splitting it into a positive semidefinite term, the Bochner sheaf Laplacian, and a block diagonal term, the Forman curvature. We show that the Bochner Laplacians form a class of cellular sheaves that extends both connection and matrix-weighted Laplacians, and generalizes signed graphs to $d$ dimensions. We give a holonomy characterization of their kernel, prove the related Cheeger inequalities, and attach to them a random walk that generalizes the Gremban expansion. For the Forman term, we prove a discrete Bochner theorem, which bounds the first cohomology of a cellular sheaf with nonnegative curvature, and we read the whole decomposition as an opinion-dynamics model. We then apply this machinery to Sheaf Neural Networks, whose learnt Laplacian is otherwise unobserved. The Bochner interpretation yields a node-level conviction score that acts as an operational importance measure under frozen-model interventions, while the Forman profile provides a local descriptor of the learnt operator.

我们将 Bochner-Weitzenböck 分解推广到胞腔层拉普拉斯算子，将其拆分为一个半正定项——Bochner 层拉普拉斯算子——以及一个块对角项——Forman 曲率。我们证明 Bochner 拉普拉斯算子构成一类胞腔层，它同时推广了连接拉普拉斯算子与矩阵加权拉普拉斯算子，并将符号图推广到 $d$ 维。我们给出其核的和乐刻画，证明相关的 Cheeger 不等式，并为其附加一个推广 Gremban 展开的随机游走。对于 Forman 项，我们证明一个离散 Bochner 定理，该定理给出具有非负曲率的胞腔层的第一上同调的界，并将整个分解解读为一个观点动力学模型。随后我们将这一机制应用于层神经网络（Sheaf Neural Networks），其学习所得的拉普拉斯算子在其他情况下是不可观测的。Bochner 解释产生一个节点级确信度得分，该得分在冻结模型干预下作为可操作的重要性度量，而 Forman 剖面则提供学习所得算子的局部描述符。

ICLHerd: Herding-Based Data Selection for LLMs with In-Context Learning as a Proxy
ICLHerd：以语境学习为代理的、基于 Herding 的大语言模型数据选择
Yuqiao Wen, Lili Mou
cs.CL · cs.AI · cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Data selection plays a central role in modern large language model training, as the quality of training data strongly influences downstream performance. A common approach is to curate a development set that encodes the desired skills (e.g., reasoning or multilinguality) and select data that are similar to them. Existing methods compute similarity using cosine distance over either the model's hidden states or gradients. However, we observe that this max-similarity strategy induces a mode-seeking bias: the selected data clusters tightly around the development samples. To address this, we propose ICLHerd, a data selection framework that leverages the von Mises-Fisher kernel to balance mode-seeking with mode-averaging. We further introduce in-context learning as a validation proxy, enabling efficient hyperparameter search over the balance trade-off. Results show that ICLHerd outperforms existing LLM data selection algorithms, highlighting the importance of balancing mode-seeking and mode-averaging.

Preference-Aware Pareto Steering for Multi-Task Speech LLMs
面向多任务语音大语言模型的偏好感知帕累托引导
Liuyuan Jiang, Vishal Sunder, Samuel Thomas, Brian Kingsbury, Jeff Kuo, Lisha Chen, George Saon
cs.CL · cs.SD
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Speech large language models (LLMs) perform multiple tasks, including automatic speech recognition (ASR), timestamp prediction (TS), and speech translation (ST). Joint training of speech LLMs creates task trade-offs, yet standard training with fixed loss weights does not generally control the resulting trade-off according to deployment preferences. To address this, we propose Endpoint-Anchored Preference-Aware Sampling Uniformly along the Pareto Front (EA-SURF), an a priori method that adapts scalarization weights so that the resulting task trade-off reflects the desired preference. EA-SURF retains the standard weighted-loss training pipeline, tracking the current model's performance relative to each task-specific reference and adapting the scalarization weights as training proceeds. We theoretically show that EA-SURF can match a desired preference, with the update becoming stationary at the target under checkable regularity conditions. Across six three-objective speech LLM requests, EA-SURF empirically converges toward the requested targets and increases endpoint-inclusive normalized hypervolume by 17.8% over fixed loss weighting.

Samee Arif, Furkan Danisman, Angana Borah, Honglak Lee, Dehan Kong, Lajanugen Logeswaran, Moontae Lee, Zhijing Jin, Rada Mihalcea
cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly operate across culturally diverse settings, yet existing evaluations largely measure cultural behavior at the output level. We introduce CultureLens, a reference-grounded benchmark and mechanistic study of how LLMs use cultural information. CultureLens contains 9,261 scenarios across 75 countries and systematically varies country, value, true-norm, and contradictory-norm evidence. Across Llama-3.1-8B, Gemma-3-12B, and Qwen-3.5-27B, stating a contradictory norm lowers aligned answers by 32-47 percentage points, even when the model answers correctly from the country alone. Mechanistically, models default to Anglophone norms when no country is given. The failure under a contradictory norm is not one of missing knowledge, as blocking the norm inside the model restores the correct answer in most cases. Models accept a stated norm according to how it is presented and not whether it is true, which leaves them most exposed to errors in retrieved content. Supervised fine-tuning with contradictory-norm examples raises aligned answers under a contradictory norm to 85-93%, including on unseen countries, at a small cost under a true norm.

大语言模型（LLMs）越来越多地在文化多样的环境中运行，然而现有评估在很大程度上仅在输出层面测量文化行为。我们引入CultureLens，这是一个基于参考的基准，也是对LLMs如何使用文化信息的机制性研究。CultureLens包含跨越75个国家的9,261个情景，并系统地变化国家、价值、真实规范和矛盾规范证据。在Llama-3.1-8B、Gemma-3-12B和Qwen-3.5-27B上，陈述一个矛盾规范会使对齐答案降低32-47个百分点，即使模型仅凭国家信息就能正确回答。从机制上看，当未给出国家时，模型默认采用英语圈规范。在矛盾规范下的失败并不是知识缺失导致的，因为在模型内部阻断该规范会在大多数情况下恢复正确答案。模型是否接受一个被陈述的规范取决于它如何被呈现，而不是它是否真实，这使得它们最容易受到检索内容中错误的影响。使用矛盾规范示例进行监督微调，将在矛盾规范下的对齐答案提高到85-93%，包括在未见过的国家上，同时在真实规范下仅有很小的代价。

Diagnostic Analysis for Large Language Model Reasoning
大语言模型推理的诊断分析
Xinyu Liu, Dongqi Fu, Jun Wu
cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Reasoning structures (e.g., chains and graphs) are increasingly used for probabilistic inference, factuality verification, and uncertainty estimation, but their structural reliability is rarely evaluated directly. We test whether this reliability holds through a proposed two-stage diagnostic evaluation in open-ended multi-hop QA. Stage 1 tests different capabilities required to construct reasoning graphs, showing that graph reliability varies with topology, prompt design, and model family. Stage 2 uses uncertainty estimation as a downstream test case. Generated-edge experiments show that graph-based computation is sensitive to upstream graph errors, with performance dropping relative to the gold-graph setting. Gold-graph experiments further show that graph structure provides little benefit when used only as prompt context, but improves the separation of correct from incorrect answers by confidence score and enables node-level diagnostics.

Target-Aware Curation of Hallucination Stress Tests for Large Language Models
面向目标模型的大型语言模型幻觉压力测试精选
Jiho Lee, Bingquan Zhang, Lin Ting Liang, Soroush Vosoughi, Weicheng Ma
cs.CL · cs.AI
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Hallucination stress tests can yield similar average scores across language models even when different prompts elicit hallucinations in each model. We develop a procedure that iteratively edits source-grounded seed prompts to expose hallucinations in a target model. An LLM editor revises each prompt in response to the target's answer and a judge's category-specific score and explanation. In the main setting, the target also receives feedback on its previous response. Experiments cover 500 seeds from seven datasets and ten topics, with intrinsic and extrinsic hallucinations evaluated across open-weight and closed-source models. Editing substantially increases judge-rated severity over the seeds. In the baseline configuration, retained responses fall in the judge's strong-hallucination bin in 77.2% of runs targeting extrinsic hallucination and 74.2% targeting intrinsic hallucination. Later editing rounds account for more than half of the mean score increase. Among 219 prompts that pass model-assisted source-validity checks, 89 elicit responses containing unsupported claims. Across five models, 200 curated prompts yield similar average severity scores, although pairwise Spearman correlations between prompt-level scores are only $ρ=0.0387$ to $0.1897$. Curated prompts can be reused across models, but their diagnostic value depends on source validity and the failures they expose in each model.

cs.CL / 36 / 2610.27269
African Languages AI Safety Readiness Report
非洲语言人工智能安全就绪度报告
Israel Abebe Azime, Jesujoba O. Alabi, Tajuddeen Gwadabe, David Ifeoluwa Adelani
cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
With the widespread adoption of large language models (LLMs) across languages and domains, AI safety has emerged as a critical global concern. However, due to resource constraints, research and development efforts tend to prioritize a limited number of high-resource languages, leaving many others, especially those spoken in Africa, underrepresented. While existing research on language "resource-ness" has largely examined whether sufficient resources are available to develop language technologies, the question of whether languages are adequately represented in AI safety research has received attention only more recently. This report examines the readiness of African languages for inclusion in AI safety discussions, drawing on existing literature and data. It considers four factors: the availability of AI-relevant resources, including text data; national AI policy support; performance on established text benchmarks; and speaker population. Based on these factors, languages are grouped into four readiness categories: fully ready, mostly ready, emerging, and foundational support needed. This classification is intended to inform the inclusion of African languages in AI safety benchmarks, highlight varying levels of preparedness, and guide strategic investment in data development, policy, and community engagement for underrepresented languages.
Chinese Translation
随着大语言模型（LLMs）在不同语言和领域中的广泛采用，人工智能安全已成为一个关键的全球性问题。然而，由于资源限制，研究与开发工作往往优先关注有限数量的高资源语言，使许多其他语言——尤其是非洲使用的语言——代表性不足。尽管现有关于语言“资源性”的研究主要考察是否有足够的资源可用于开发语言技术，但语言在人工智能安全研究中是否得到充分表征这一问题直到最近才受到关注。本报告基于现有文献和数据，考察非洲语言被纳入人工智能安全讨论的就绪程度。报告考虑四个因素：与人工智能相关的资源（包括文本数据）的可获得性；国家人工智能政策支持；在既有文本基准上的表现；以及使用者人口规模。基于这些因素，各语言被划分为四个就绪度类别：完全就绪、基本就绪、新兴，以及需要基础性支持。该分类旨在为将非洲语言纳入人工智能安全基准提供参考，凸显各语言准备程度的不同，并指导针对代表性不足语言在数据开发、政策和社区参与方面的战略性投资。

cs.CL / 37 / 2610.27304
Global Security Blind Spots: Translation as a Safety Bypass in Low-Resource Languages
全球安全盲点：翻译作为低资源语言中的安全绕过
Jalil Alva, David Harper, Abigail E. Thornton, Rafael S. Villalobos Alva, Leonardo Kenji Minemura Suazo, Konstantinos Karageorgos, Diego Velazquez, Sergio A. Serrano, Marvin Vargas Flores, Aaron Schliem, Fernando F. Migone
cs.CL · cs.AI · cs.CR · cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language models are deployed globally, yet safety alignment and evaluation remain concentrated in English: harmful requests refused in English can elicit unsafe completions when translated into low-resource languages. We evaluate ten widely deployed LLMs across 79 languages (English plus 78 low-resource) under a translation-bypass threat model, using a metric conditioned on English safety, which separates translation bypass from unsafety already present in English. English safety does not transfer reliably: conditioned on safe English completions, mean bypass rates range from 21.9% to 44.4%. Bypass risk concentrates in a subset of language families, a pattern broadly shared across models. The shared ordering is confounded with translation degeneracy, but its variation across models is significant and survives every control we apply. We also show that per-model bypass rates do not identify a stable ranking: nine of ten models change rank across three conditioning schemes that estimate the same quantity, with no change to any underlying response.

DStill: Trajectory Consistency Distillation for Accelerated One-Step Drafting in Block Diffusion Speculative Decoding
DStill：用于块扩散投机解码中加速一步草稿生成的轨迹一致性蒸馏
Shreyas Kulkarni, Uttam Gurram, Madhav Kanda, Krishna Teja Chitty Venkata, Shichu Chen, Kartik Balasubramaniam, Supriyo Chakraborty, Sambit Sahu
cs.CL · cs.LG
diffusionlarge language model
扩散模型相关
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Block-diffusion speculative decoding accelerates large language model inference by drafting multiple tokens in parallel. However, one-step drafting in discrete diffusion is limited by token factorization error: each token is predicted from the same masked block, without conditioning on the tokens selected at other positions in that step. This can produce inconsistent drafts and reduce acceptance length. Iterative refinement mitigates this limitation by conditioning later predictions on previously committed tokens, though additional passes increase drafting cost. To address this trade-off between draft fidelity and inference latency, we introduce DStill, a two-stage framework that distills a target-conditioned drafter's own multi-step refinement into one-step drafting. We first train the drafter to complete partially revealed blocks, then use its refinement trajectories to train a student to predict the final completion in one pass. Using a curriculum that gradually transitions from partial to fully masked inputs, we successfully transfer the multi-step refinement capabilities into one step. Across reasoning, math, code benchmarks on three model families DStill improves acceptance length by up to 28% and speedup by up to 25% over one-step DFlash, achieving up to 6.45x speedup over auto-regressive decoding.
Chinese Translation

cs.CL / 39 / 2610.27455
Detecting Errors in Large Language Model Responses: The Incremental Predictive Value of Hidden States
检测大型语言模型回答中的错误：隐藏状态的增量预测价值
Ningzhi Li, Xiaojun Ma, Xiaofei Wang
cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Although large language models support a wide range of tasks, hallucinations remain a major obstacle to user trust. When a model generates an answer, both its internal processing and final output vary with the question. Internal states are often expected to offer richer signals for hallucination detection. However, studies using these states typically report their standalone discrimination performance, while output-side comparisons often use simple baselines with weaker modeling capacity. We integrate output-side information available at inference time into a combined baseline and compare detection performance before and after adding hidden states under identical data splits and evaluation rules. Experiments cover open-ended generation and constrained multiple-choice tasks across different models. Adding hidden states improves AUROC by approximately 0.004 and 0.039 on the two tasks, respectively. Hidden states thus provide additional predictive information, but strong standalone detection performance can still yield only limited additional gains.

cs.CL / 40 / 2610.27566
Learned Readout Tokens for Extracting Large Language Model Confidence
用于提取大语言模型置信度的学习读出令牌
Nima Seifi, Martin Ester
cs.CL · cs.AI · cs.LG
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used within everyday applications where their responses have significant downstream impacts. For responsible deployment of such systems, we desire insight into how much we can trust their individual outputs. A popular approach for estimating LLM confidence is to train probes on the hidden states of the LLM's tokens to predict the correctness of the model's output. These probes typically read hidden states from tokens that are already in the model's vocabulary. In this work, we introduce a new approach to confidence probes that learn a new readout token and utilize its hidden states to train the probe. We show that our learned readout approach ScratchProbe outperforms its existing-token counterpart on a variety of datasets and LLMs. We also extend our method to a multi-token approach which we show provides further performance improvements. Finally, since the learned readout changes only the position a probe reads from, any existing probe can adopt it. Applied to a state-of-the-art probe, it improves AUROC on every backbone, in domain and out of domain.

cs.CL / 41 / 2610.27577
Why Static Probes Fail: Context Determines Deception Feature Composition
静态探针为何失效：上下文决定欺骗特征组成
Yao Huang, Siyuan Chen, Zhenghan Zhou, Yinpeng Dong
cs.CL
large language model
大语言模型相关
Abstract
With increasing autonomy, Large Language Models (LLMs) may engage in deceptive behaviors, such as scheming to pursue misaligned goals or sandbagging to escape oversight. Monitoring outputs alone is insufficient, as models can produce seemingly benign responses while harboring misaligned internal objectives. While mechanistic approaches like linear probing are promising, they rely on the assumption that deception corresponds to a single direction in representation space. We demonstrate that such single-direction probes fail to generalize across diverse deception scenarios. To bridge this gap, we propose representing deception as a multi-dimensional subspace rather than a single direction. Our method utilizes iterative orthogonal decomposition to identify complementary directions that capture distinct facets of deceptive intent. To effectively leverage these directions for detection, we find that static combinations prove brittle due to strong domain dependence across different scenarios. We therefore introduce a domain-adaptive gating mechanism that dynamically composes the extracted directions through few-shot adaptation at test time. With only 10 examples, our approach achieves an average AUROC of 0.97 and 94% recall at 5% FPR across all evaluated datasets, substantially outperforming existing methods.

随着自主性的不断增强，大型语言模型（LLM）可能会表现出欺骗行为，例如为追求与目标不一致的目标而进行谋划，或为逃避监督而故意保留能力（sandbagging）。仅监控输出是不够的，因为模型可能在怀有与目标不一致的内部目标的同时生成看似无害的回应。虽然线性探针等机制性方法很有前景，但它们依赖于一个假设：欺骗对应于表示空间中的单一方向。我们证明，这种单一方向探针无法在多样化的欺骗场景中泛化。为弥合这一差距，我们提出将欺骗表示为多维子空间，而不是单一方向。我们的方法利用迭代正交分解来识别能够捕捉欺骗意图不同侧面的互补方向。为了有效利用这些方向进行检测，我们发现静态组合由于不同场景之间存在强烈的领域依赖性而显得脆弱。因此，我们引入了一种领域自适应门控机制，通过在测试时进行少样本自适应来动态组合所提取的方向。仅使用10个示例，我们的方法在所有评估数据集上就达到了平均AUROC 0.97以及在5% FPR下94%的召回率，大幅优于现有方法。

cs.CL / 42 / 2610.27580
Factual Access States in Diffusion Language Models: From Mechanism to Knowledge Editing and Retrieval
扩散语言模型中的事实访问状态：从机制到知识编辑与检索
Yuchen Guo, Zhuoyuan Mao, Yiwen Guo
cs.CL · cs.AI · cs.IR · cs.LG
diffusion
扩散模型相关
Abstract
Factual recall is a lookup: some representation inside the network serves as the key, and what that key is made of decides which queries can retrieve the fact, what an edit must cover, and what a retriever can read. We call it the factual access state. In autoregressive (AR) models the subject position enriches attributes largely independently of the relation, and relation-specific selection happens later, at the readout position. In masked diffusion language models (DLMs) we find the state is assembled differently, and much earlier: in the first attention layer the wording of the relation is routed into the position of whichever entity is visible and the early feed-forward layers look the fact up on this fused representation. The state therefore varies with the relation's surface form and with the query direction, so the queries about one fact occupy a region of state space rather than a point, and an operation on the fact succeeds only for queries that enter it. We treat the state as an interface to a DLM's factual knowledge, and put it to two uses. Writing to the state gives a knowledge editor: from one declarative statement, Multi-View Edit fits one shared value per direction across that region and installs it in the early-MLP block, preserving source-prompt reliability while substantially improving paraphrase and reverse question answering, where AR editors gain near zero. Reading it suggests a complementary use: the state at each entity position can serve as a relation-specific retrieval vector with no training, returning both pieces of evidence for two-entity queries on which pooled, prompted and lexical retrievers almost never return both.

TeCoP: Accelerating Diffusion Large Language Model Decoding via Tentative Context Pipelining
